note: AI-generated from validated analysis. Trust: validated = holds out-of-sample (LOO); directional = real but small-n / weak; craft = sound judgment that didn't move our stats; method = how we work.

findings.title: Stayed-to-watch is THE lever
findings.body: Shorts above ~75% stayed-to-watch get roughly 4× the views. It's the single biggest thing you control. (Studio-only metric — paste it in per video.)

findings.title: The opening visual decides the swipe
findings.body: Decided in ~1 second — too fast to hear words. Drivers (short videos): a face in frame 1 (ρ +0.78), a 'what is that?' mystery object / low clarity (ρ −0.73), and quick cuts (ρ +0.65).

findings.title: Swipe prediction model v2
findings.body: Predicted stayed-to-watch = 2·face + (5 − clarity), calibrated to your data. Honest accuracy ±3.8 points (leave-one-out).

findings.title: Watch-through = front-loaded audio energy
findings.body: Open loud and DON'T ramp up. Short: AVD ≈ 90.25 − 134·audio_buildup (±2.1). Long: 87.48 + 35.46·loud_first2s − 0.095·brightness (±3.0). AVD is more predictable than swipe.

findings.title: Views = topic & reach, not craft
findings.body: Nothing about the opening or script predicts views. What does: format/topic — comparison/versus & knockoff beat single-object demos ~23× — and channel reach. Confirmed on 100 competitor videos. To grow views, pick the format.

findings.title: Always judge within a length bucket
findings.body: Rules differ by length. Avg-view-% target ≈ 94% for short (20–35s) vs ~84% for long (45–65s). The swipe drivers matter most for short videos.

findings.title: Open with a statement, not a question
findings.body: Opening on a direct question consistently underperforms; lead with a statement (ideally one that goes against common belief). Never narrate a 'nothing's happening' state.

findings.title: Script wording is weak on watch-through
findings.body: We scored every second's script meaning against the real retention curve. The effect on AVD is weak-to-undetectable at current data size — not in the model yet. Revisit with more videos + finer retention.
findings.evidence: 14 videos, 529 seconds, ρ≈0 after position control

findings.title: Color / brightness = craft, not a swipe lever
findings.body: Measured brightness/contrast/colorfulness don't move the swipe in our data (≈0). Competitor top-view openings are brighter & clearer (engagement, not swipe). Keep it bright & high-contrast as craft — it just hasn't earned a coefficient.
findings.evidence: ρ≈0 vs swipe; competitor +0.21 on likes

findings.title: Top channels never open on dead air
findings.body: Across 100 competitor shorts, the highest-view openings have ~0% dead-air and ~3% null-state narration. Both our data and theirs agree: cut any inert/'nothing happens' opening.

findings.title: We measure 37 variables, use the validated few
findings.body: Every video is scored on 37 variables and all are tested. Only the leave-one-out-validated ones earn a coefficient (2 for swipe, audio for AVD) — adding more overfits at small n. The way to use more variables is more videos.

findings.title: Retention curve ≠ views
findings.body: A viral video dilutes into a broader audience, lowering raw retention — so the retention curve doesn't predict views. Use relative-retention, and optimize the swipe & AVD levers instead.

findings.title: Reach dominates the view gap
findings.body: Competitor median views ≈53× ours, and their worst video beats our median — that's subscribers + algorithm + topic, not per-second craft. Don't judge a script by views; judge it by same-channel watch-through.
